Extract from Daily Intelligence Report dated 3/10/36
----

Communist Propaganda - two arrests
Acting on the authority of warrants issued at the
instance of the Soongwu Garrison Commander's Headquarters,
the Municipal Police on October 2, 1936, raided houses No.
363, Lane 361, Myburgh Road, and No.1407, Zih yih Li,
Robison Road, and arrested one communist suspect at each
place. A quantity of communist literature was also
seized at the former address.
The two accused will appear before Court on October
3 when application will be made for their detention.

Communist Propaganda - court proceedings.
The case against the two communist suspects who
were arrested on October 2 (Vide I.R. 3/10/36) was concluded
in the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court on October 3, when
they were extradited to the Chinese Authorities.

IN THE ALLEGED 2ND S.S.D. COURT

Mr. Kum appeared for the S.M. Council.
Messrs. Tsang, Lah Lum & Yue Liu Ting for accused.
(At the opening session, Judge Hsiao sat alone at Court)

Proceedings.
Mr. Kum :- The accused is wanted by the Shanghai and
Woosung Garrison Headquarters on suspicion of being a communist.
At about 1a.m. on 2-10-36, a representative of the said Head-
quarters and members of the Special Branch, S.M.P., came to
Linza Station, and the former asked for assistance to execute two
warrants for the arrest of a communist and for the search of XX
premises at house 363, Lane 361, Tyburgh Rd. Assistance was
rendered, and the accused was arrested. In a drawer of a desk sat
by him was seized a quantity of communistic literature. He was
implicated by another communist who had already been arrested by
the Chinese Authorities, whose representative is in Court to-day,
asking for the handing over of the accused.

U.M.C. 292:- At about 1a.m. yesterday, D.S. Jones of
the Special Branch and a representative of the Shanghai & Woosung
Garrison Headquarters came to the Station and asked for assistance
to search house 363, Lane 361, Tyburgh Rd, and to arrest and seize
any communist or communistic literature found therein. I and a
party rendered the necessary assistance and accused was arrested.
The literature was found inside a drawer of the accused.

Judge Hsiao to accused:-
Q. Do you hear the evidence of the Municipal Advocate and the

A. Yes, but one of them does not belong to me.
        Yang Voong Lee:- I am a representative of the Shanghai

named Yang Voong Min was arrested, and on his person was found

warrant were then applied for and at 10a.m. yesterday, with the
assistance of ......, we went to search premises at lane 361/563
Kyber(h Rd. We found the accused there and he stated that he
was named Lee. Questioned regarding the man Tsai Kyi, he said
that he was not called Tsai. There was a lawyer named Tang also

The prisoner also stated the position of the desk at which the

Several cards in the name of "Tsai Pei Kyi" were also found.
Accused then admitted that he was named Tsai, and the prisoner

Judge Yock to accused:-
Q. Are you a member of the National Salvation Union?
A. No, I am a member of National Distress Educational Society.
Q. What is the work of the Society?
A. I don't know exactly, but it is for educational purposes.
Q. Does the seized literature belong to you?
A. The communism book belongs to me.
Q. Are these photos yours?
A. No, they belong to my friend. The handbills belong to
another friend named Teang who placed them in my drawer.
Q. Why do you join the Society?
A. At first, I thought that they would obtain a job for me.

Representative of the Chinese Authorities re-outlined
his evidence as given above.

Judge Yock to Mr. Lum:-
Q. What is the opinion of the Police regarding this case?
A. The Police first intended to ask for a remand, but in view
of the fact that this case is quite clear and that the Chinese
Authorities will continue further enquiries in order to effect
the arrest of other communists, I have no objection to his
being handed over immediately.

Procurator:- Accused can be handed over immediately.
Mr. Yee:- There is no such evidence to prove that ac-
cused is a communist. I ask that the request of the Chinese
Authorities be dismissed.

Tsai Pei Kyi (蔡培基). age 22.
Shanghai                                      D, S. Jones
Sinza Stn,              2,10,36,                    Clerk Z,O,Zung

    From the age of 7 to 18 years I studied at various primary
schools in Shanghai, The last school I attended was the Tsing
Kyung(精勤) Educational Institute, West Gate, where I remained
for 2½ years,    I reside with my father at Lane 38, No, 61,
Myburgh Road.
    On leaving school I became an apprentice at the Gold Bar
Exchange(        ), corner of Kiukiang Road, the Bund,  After
six months the broker who employed me went bankrupt and I lost
my job,  A few months later I obtained my present position as
clerk to lawyer Yu Cheng Ting(何待鼎 ). 365 Myburgh Road,  I was
never actually in the employ of Sung Ih Foo (沈一夫 ).  The
latter. who is a chartered accountant, shared  the same office
as my employer Yu Cheng Ting,  At the beginning of this year
Sung Ih Foo left for Hankow and is no longer connected with this
office,
    I am engaged on clerical work. chiefly copying petitions to
the court.  For this work I am paid $6.00 a month and receive
a commission on each case handled by my employer,
    My father, Tsai Zang Tseh(蔡尚爵 ), is employed as a clerk
at the Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China, the Bund
He has been there for about 15 years,
    I am not a communist, neither do I believe in communism. In
January of this year I joined the National Crisis Educational
Society, the object of which is to acquaint the people with the
present national crisis,  I took no part in the activities of
this society,
    The communistic and anti-Government literature found in my
desk were handed to me to by one Tsang( 张   ), whose address I

-2-
do not know. He is a member of the above society, His last
visit to me was at my office in April last.
The diary containing the anti-Chiang Kai Shek notes is mine,
I made these notes when attending the various lectures of the
National Crisis Educational Society, There is no fixed place
of meeting for this society, The last lecture I attended
was towards the end of April. It was held in the Bei Ming
( 北 明 ) Girls' School, corner of Connaught and Hart Roads.
This meeting was stopped by the Settlement Police soon after it
started, There were no arrests made.
The organizer of the National Crisis Educational Society
was one Dau Ying Ts ( 陶 行 知 ), an educationalist who is now
studying abroad,
